scenes.title: Cloud Networking & Security Deep Dive
scenes.narration: Advanced cloud networking secures data platforms by keeping traffic private, layering defenses, and eliminating exposure to the public internet wherever possible.

scenes.title: Layered Network Defenses
bullets: Private subnets keep data stores off the public internet entirely.
Private endpoints let you reach managed services without traversing the internet.
Security groups and network ACLs enforce least-privilege traffic rules in depth.
scenes.narration: Strong network security is built in layers. Placing data stores in private subnets removes any direct internet path. Private endpoints then let those resources reach managed services over the provider's backbone instead of the public internet. Security groups and network ACLs add fine-grained, least-privilege rules so only intended traffic ever flows.

scenes.title: Private Path to a Managed Service
steps: Compute sits in a private subnet
Request goes to a VPC endpoint
Traffic stays on the cloud backbone
scenes.narration: Consider a job reaching a managed service securely. The compute runs in a private subnet with no internet route. Its request travels to a VPC endpoint, which keeps the traffic entirely on the provider's private backbone. The service responds the same way, so sensitive data never touches the public internet at any point.

scenes.title: Public Access vs. Private Access
scenes.narration: Reaching services over the public internet enlarges your attack surface and can incur egress charges. Private access via endpoints keeps traffic on the cloud backbone, shrinking exposure and often reducing cost at the same time. For any sensitive data platform, private connectivity should be the default.

scenes.title: Restricting a Bucket to a VPC Endpoint
scenes.narration: This bucket policy locks storage access to a single VPC endpoint. The statement denies all S3 actions unless the request arrives through the specified endpoint, using a condition on the source VPC endpoint identifier. Even a valid credential cannot read the bucket from outside your private network, layering network control on top of IAM.

scenes.text: Defense in depth means private subnets, private endpoints, and tight traffic rules together — keep sensitive data off the public internet by default.
scenes.narration: Real cloud security is layered: private subnets, private endpoints, and least-privilege traffic rules reinforcing one another. Keeping sensitive data off the public internet by default is the foundation everything else builds on.
